Reconstructing the Douay–Rheims: a corroborated dual-edition digital critical text

Modern (idx 108) & archaic-diplomatic (idx 109) editions as deterministic projections of one independence-weighted basis database

SourcesMethodsResultsDiscussionLimitationsReproducibilityReferences

Abstract

We reconstruct two facsimile-grade digital editions of the Douay–Rheims Bible — a modern (idx 108) and an archaic-diplomatic (idx 109) rendering — as deterministic projections of a single basis database of 37,185 scripture verses assembled from 18 witnesses across 7 independent lineages. Every verse is corroborated across all attesting witnesses and assigned a consensus confidence tier; 82.1% reach the high tier (mean cross-witness agreement 0.810). A re-detection gate confirms 100% coordinate round-trip (Gate P1 = PASS). The two editions share skeleton, apparatus placement and element structure exactly and differ only in a final spelling/typeset layer, so their diff isolates precisely the orthographic delta. A documented bidirectional spelling-glyph model folds the two surfaces to a neutral skeleton: post-fold word correspondence is 0.759 mean Jaccard (§6.2), and both editions corroborate against an independent third-party OCR of the original 1582/1609/1610 print at 87.76% (archaic) / 90.66% (modern) recall with zero genuine content-word discrepancies (§6.3).

Introduction

The reconstruction follows one paradigm: detect everywhere → consensus-generate → re-detect to confirm. Each element is detected across every witness that attests it; a consensus surface is called with independence-weighted confidence; the assembled basis is then re-detected to prove a lossless round-trip. Scans of the original print are the layout authority. One basis yields two renderings — spelling/typeset is a final layer, not a separate transcription — so both editions draw on all sources. The visual grammar here is a genome browser's: confidence tiers band a chromosome ideogram, independent-witness depth is read depth, and source disagreements surface as variant pileups.

Methods

Skeleton. A canonical coordinate grid of 37,185 scripture verses plus 102 apparatus items and 82 structural nodes anchors every witness to a shared address space.

Per-source detection & consensus. Each witness is aligned by content-anchored matching; a consensus surface is called per coordinate with an agreement score, support depth and independent depth. Confidence tiers: high 30,522 / moderate 6,424 / low 239.

Layout grounding. Apparatus placement and book/tome ordering are grounded in the archive.org page scans: 17 of 26 apparatus slots are scan-grounded with committed header crops (6 co-located, 1 unlocatable, 2 inventoried).

Conversion model (§6.1). A documented bidirectional spelling-glyph fold (long-ſ↔s, æ↔ae, œ↔oe, u/v, i/j, vv↔w, &↔and, period spellings) reduces both surfaces to a neutral skeleton for comparison; archaic rendering restores each form from the archaic witness, never a lossy back-transform.

Results

Coverage & confidence. 82.1% of verses reach the high tier; independent depth distribution (verses corroborated by k independent lineages): 1=239, 2=8,680, 3=15,472, 4=12,794.

Source coverage & read depth. Read depth (attesting witnesses, up to five) and independent depth (independent lineages, up to four) diverge by exactly one step because the modern transcription backbone (madueke_a) and the apparatus backbone (sabates_a) share the Madueke lineage; consensus weights by independent lineage so a witness family never corroborates itself. The source-track browser reads position-by-position: Genesis 1 carries all five witnesses, while an ocr-only prophetic book (Isaie 1) falls to the three witnesses whose lineages reach it — the read-depth collapse made visible.

Per-book contribution. Resolved to the book, the modern transcription backbone (madueke_a), the apparatus backbone (sabates_a) and the fresh OCR span the whole canon, while the archaic diplomatic witnesses (s-dismas, odr-com) cover Genesis through the sapiential books and fall to zero across the prophets and appendix — the ocr-only stratum, shown grey:

Consensus & variant structure. Where witnesses disagree, the pileup lays each surface reading under the called consensus. The largest disagreements are not OCR noise but versification offsets: a witness numbering under the alternate Vulgate convention reads the neighbouring verse (e.g. the odr-com and s-dismas witnesses at the Matthew 18:33 locus read verse 34), which the independence-weighted consensus resolves to the majority-attested reading and records as a versification adjudication case (§6.2). Genuine fresh-OCR garble (e.g. the ocr-only Isaie locus) surfaces as a single low-Jaccard read against otherwise-agreeing witnesses.

Apparatus inclusion. 25 of 26 reference documents are included (1 excluded, honestly flagged); all 76 books carry apparatus-channel attestation. Two witnesses supply the apparatus — Sabates as the backbone across all five channels, odr-com supplementing the book arguments and sidecar notes:

Scan-grounded placement. Every apparatus slot is located in the original print: 17 grounded with a committed header crop, 6 co-located on a shared leaf, 2 inventoried (OCR-attested, leaf pending) and 1 unlocatable (honestly excluded). Discussion

Rendering fidelity is governed by archaic-witness coverage. Where s-dismas contributes a clean diplomatic transcription, the archaic surface folds almost exactly onto the modern one and corroborates the independent print as a true cross-witness check. The ocr-only books (Isaie, Ecclesiasticus, Zacharias, 4-Esdras, the minor prophets) carry the fresh-OCR long-ſ→f misread; the §6.2 fold deliberately keeps f and s distinct so this surfaces as a measured residual rather than being masked. The §6.3 severe residual tail is not OCR noise but verse-numbering divergence in the well-attested books — chiefly the Vulgate convention of numbering a psalm's title as verse 1 — recorded as a versification adjudication set.

Limitations

The archaic surface has coverage gaps (199 modern-present coordinates with no archaic witness) rendered from the modern surface and flagged, and a set of archaic-only coordinates deferred as a versification adjudication set. For the ocr-only books, archaic-vs-print recall is partially self-referential (the surface derives from the same OCR family); the modern-vs-print recall is the independent signal there. The masked editorial apparatus is shared between editions (modern witness); an archaic apparatus witness is a documented follow-up.
